correctness.rationale: For arbitrary abelian A with N>=4, the four support regions give an exact convolution energy formula. The eight-term identity follows algebraically and all terms are nonnegative by finite Cauchy--Schwarz, inversion-pair arithmetic and triangle inequality; coefficient 2N-6-2/(N-1)>0. Equality forces GH=0, then exact finite Fourier Plancherel forces one nonzero transform coefficient, i.e. a scalar character on one whole axis. Normalizations yield N^3/(2N-1)^2. The direct checker tests cyclic/noncyclic groups and exact identity; finite tests are corroboration, not proof. N=3 excluded with exact counterexample.

value.rationale: A canonical reducible finite-field curve lies outside established field-uniform algebraic-curve restriction theory. The exact norm for every finite abelian group of order at least four, all equality functions and an explicit nonnegative eight-part stability defect provide information not afforded by qualitative no-linear-factor criteria or flat-input energy counts. The strict rigidity transition after the exceptional order-three case is structurally meaningful. No paper-sized corollary is asserted or required.
